import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 394

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/394](https://www.erdosproblems.com/394)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [ErHa78] Erdős, P. and Hall, R. R., On some unconventional problems on the divisors of integers.
  J. Austral. Math. Soc. Ser. A (1978), 479--485.
-/

open Nat Filter Finset
open scoped Asymptotics Topology Nat

namespace Erdos394

/--
Let $t_k(n)$ denote the least $m$ such that $n\mid m(m+1)(m+2)\cdots (m+k-1).$
-/
noncomputable def t (k n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf { m : ℕ | 0 < m ∧ n ∣ ∏ i ∈ range k, (m + i) }

/-- `t k n = v` when `v` works and nothing positive below it does. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem t_eq_of {n k v : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v)
    (hdvd : n ∣ ∏ i ∈ range k, (v + i))
    (hlt : ∀ m ∈ range v, 0 < m → ¬ (n ∣ ∏ i ∈ range k, (m + i))) :
    t k n = v := by
  refine le_antisymm (Nat.sInf_le ⟨hv, hdvd⟩) ?_
  by_contra! hc
  have hne : { m : ℕ | 0 < m ∧ n ∣ ∏ i ∈ range k, (m + i) }.Nonempty := ⟨v, hv, hdvd⟩
  obtain ⟨hpos, hd⟩ := Nat.sInf_mem hne
  exact hlt _ (mem_range.mpr hc) hpos hd

/-- The least positive multiple of `n` is `n`, so `t 1 n = n`. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem t_one {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : t 1 n = n := by
  refine le_antisymm (Nat.sInf_le ⟨hn, by simp⟩) ?_
  have hne : { m : ℕ | 0 < m ∧ n ∣ ∏ i ∈ range 1, (m + i) }.Nonempty := ⟨n, hn, by simp⟩
  obtain ⟨hpos, hd⟩ := Nat.sInf_mem hne
  rw [prod_range_one, add_zero] at hd
  exact Nat.le_of_dvd hpos hd

/--
Is it true that $\sum_{n\leq x}t_2(n)\ll \frac{x^2}{(\log x)^c}$ for some $c>0$?
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/williamjblair/lean-proofs/blob/4f915a323443bfb1709a6805a013812016dca88a/starfleet/erdos-394/Research/FirstQuestion.lean"]
theorem erdos_394.parts.i :
    answer(True) ↔
      ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), (fun x ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊,
      (t 2 n : ℝ)) ≪ (fun x ↦ x ^ 2 / (Real.log x) ^ c) := by
  sorry

/--
Is it true that, for $k\geq 2$, $\sum_{n\leq x}t_{k+1}(n) =o\left(\sum_{n\leq x}t_k(n)\right)?$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/williamjblair/lean-proofs/blob/4f915a323443bfb1709a6805a013812016dca88a/starfleet/erdos-394/Research/DenseHierarchyLittleO.lean"]
theorem erdos_394.parts.ii :
    answer(True) ↔
      ∀ k ≥ 2, (fun (x : ℝ) ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊,
      (t (k + 1) n : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun (x : ℝ) ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊,
      (t k n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
In [ErGr80] they mention a conjecture of Erdős that the sum is $o(x^2)$. This was proved by Erdős
and Hall [ErHa78], who proved that in fact
$\sum_{n\leq x}t_2(n)\ll \frac{\log\log\log x}{\log\log x}x^2.$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_394.variants.hall_bound :
    (fun x ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊, (t 2 n : ℝ)) ≪
    (fun x ↦ x ^ 2 * (Real.log (Real.log (Real.log x)) / Real.log (Real.log x))) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Hall conjecture that the sum is $o(x^2/(\log x)^c)$ for any $c<\log 2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_394.variants.hall_conjecture :
    ∀ c < Real.log 2, (fun x ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊,
    (t 2 n : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
    (fun x ↦ x ^ 2 / (Real.log x) ^ c) := by
  sorry

/--
Since $t_2(p)=p-1$ for prime $p$ it is trivial that $\sum_{n\leq x}t_2(n)\gg \frac{x^2}{\log x}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_394.variants.lower_bound :
    (fun x ↦ x ^ 2 / Real.log x) ≪
    (fun x ↦ ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊, (t 2 n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
They ask about the behaviour of $t_{n-3}(n!)$ and also ask whether, for infinitely many $n$,
$t_k(n!)< t_{k-1}(n!)-1$ for all $1\leq k < n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_394.variants.factorial_gap_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      Set.Infinite { n : ℕ | ∀ k, 2 ≤ k → k < n →
      t k (n !) < t (k - 1) (n !) - 1 } := by
  sorry

set_option maxRecDepth 20000 in
/--
They proved (with Selfridge) that this holds for $n=10$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_394.variants.factorial_gap_10 :
    ∀ (k : ℕ), 2 ≤ k → k < 10 →
    t k (10 !) <
    t (k - 1) (10 !) - 1 := by
  have h1 : t 1 (10 !) = 3628800 := by rw [t_one] <;> norm_num [Nat.factorial]
  have h2 : t 2 (10 !) = 512000 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by native_decide) (by native_decide)
  have h3 : t 3 (10 !) = 6398 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by native_decide) (by native_decide)
  have h4 : t 4 (10 !) = 5373 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by native_decide) (by native_decide)
  have h5 : t 5 (10 !) = 348 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by decide) (by decide)
  have h6 : t 6 (10 !) = 160 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by decide) (by decide)
  have h7 : t 7 (10 !) = 30 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by decide) (by decide)
  have h8 : t 8 (10 !) = 9 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by decide) (by decide)
  have h9 : t 9 (10 !) = 2 := by
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]; exact t_eq_of (by norm_num) (by decide) (by decide)
  intro k hk2 hk10
  interval_cases k <;> simp_all

end Erdos394

findings.description: The docstring says the gaps hold for all `1 ≤ k < n`, whereas the Lean statement correctly uses `2 ≤ k < n`. The original paper excludes k = 1. With this file's definition, including k = 1 would invoke `t 0 (n!) = 0` for n ≥ 2 and make the gap condition impossible. This is a documentation error, not an error in the Lean proposition.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Hall, “On some unconventional problems on the divisors of integers” (1978), p. 481, immediately before equation (1), quantifies over indices `1 < i ≤ n−1` and then records the n = 10 example with Selfridge: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1978-26.pdf . The secondary webpage https://www.erdosproblems.com/394 prints `1 ≤ k < n`, apparently the transcription error copied into the docstring.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring's `$1\leq k < n$` to `$2\leq k < n$`. Leave the Lean statement unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The repository's `≪` notation fixes x to ℕ, so this is an integer-cutoff estimate rather than an estimate over real x.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The summatory function at real x equals its value at ⌊x⌋₊. For every fixed real c, the comparison function G_c(x) = x²/(log x)^c satisfies G_c(⌊x⌋₊) ~ G_c(x) as x → ∞. Consequently the natural-cutoff and real-cutoff big-O estimates are equivalent, with the same existential range c > 0. Proved as `Review394.parts_i_nat_real_iff` in /workspace/review/reformulations.lean.

reformulations.difference: The `≪` notation states the Hall bound along natural rather than real cutoffs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing G(x) = x² log log log x / log log x, the floor function and each relevant iterated logarithm are asymptotically equivalent to their unrounded counterparts. Thus G(⌊x⌋₊) ~ G(x). Together with the exact floor dependence of the summatory function, this transfers the bound in both directions. Proved as `Review394.hall_bound_nat_real_iff`.

reformulations.difference: The lower bound is expressed using natural cutoffs through `≪`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For G(x) = x²/log x, G(⌊x⌋₊) ~ G(x), while the summatory function is unchanged by replacing x with its natural floor. Therefore G = O(S) along natural cutoffs is equivalent to the same lower bound along real cutoffs. Proved as `Review394.lower_bound_nat_real_iff`.

reformulations.difference: The 1978 paper phrases the proposed improvement using big-O bounds for every fixed exponent below log 2; the Lean statement, like the Erdős Problems webpage, uses little-o for every real c < log 2.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any c < log 2, choose max(c,0) < d < log 2. The big-O estimate with exponent d implies the little-o estimate with exponent c because G_d(x)/G_c(x) = (log x)^(c−d) → 0. Conversely little-o implies big-O. This also explains why including nonpositive c adds no strength. Both versions of the family equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/reformulations.lean.

review.notes:
All ten declarations were checked. No mathematical misformalization was found. The defining minimum is nonempty for positive k,n because m=n works; its empty-set defaults do not affect the problem statements. Scratch proofs check the zero cases and show that the natural-number gap inequality is equivalent to the intended integer inequality. Finite searches reproduced all nine displayed values of t_k(10!).

The webpage still displays OPEN and reports its last edit as 28 October 2025. Nevertheless, the file's solved/True/formal_proof records are substantiated by its explicit external proof citations: I rebuilt the 101 dependency modules needed for both targets and proved bridges to the exact FC propositions. Both external theorems and both bridges have only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] as axioms. Building the Lean 4.31 sources under the supplied Lean 4.33 required backward-transparency compatibility options, without changing their source statements or proofs. Thus the older webpage banner is not evidence that the FC solved records should be reverted; the webpage's status appears not to have incorporated these proofs.

The inline factorial_gap_10 proof has the expected six native_decide-generated axioms, no sorryAx, and its numerical values were independently reproduced. Experiments and audits are under /workspace/review; the reviewed file remains identical to the specified commit.
